description: Graduate course on how robots decide where to move and how to handle objects: configuration space, search and sampling-based planners, trajectory optimisation, differential kinematics, grasping, contact-rich tasks and mobile manipulation. Students step through planners, implement them in code on arms and mobile bases, and benchmark them in a final project.
modelledOn: Lynch and Park, Modern Robotics: Mechanics, Planning, and Control
Siciliano et al., Robotics: Modelling, Planning and Control
Choset et al., Principles of Robot Motion
outcomes: Construct the configuration space of a robot and formulate a motion planning problem with collision constraints.
Implement and compare search-based and sampling-based planners, stating their completeness and optimality guarantees.
Generate smooth, feasible trajectories by time parametrisation and trajectory optimisation.
Control a redundant manipulator with differential inverse kinematics, handling singularities and secondary tasks.
Evaluate grasps with friction-cone and force-closure analysis and plan pick-and-place tasks.
Benchmark planners rigorously and critique recent literature on contact-rich and mobile manipulation.

units.title: Configuration space and problem formulation
topics: Kinematics review: forward kinematics, Denavit-Hartenberg parameters and the Jacobian
Configuration space: obstacles in C-space, topology of SO(2), SE(2) and joint spaces
Minkowski sums: translating polygon robots among polygon obstacles
Collision detection: bounding volumes, the GJK algorithm and signed distance fields
Problem classes: holonomic versus nonholonomic, completeness, optimality and computational complexity

units.title: Search-based and combinatorial planning
topics: Graph search for planning: grids, Dijkstra, A-star and admissible heuristics
Incremental replanning with D-star Lite for changing maps
Roadmaps and cell decomposition: visibility graphs and trapezoidal decomposition
Artificial potential fields, local minima and navigation functions
State lattices and car-like paths: Dubins and Reeds-Shepp curves
Bug algorithms for planning with only local sensing

units.title: Sampling-based planning
topics: Probabilistic roadmaps: construction, query and lazy collision checking
Rapidly-exploring random trees and RRT-Connect; Voronoi bias
Asymptotically optimal planners: RRT-star and PRM-star
Probabilistic completeness, narrow passages and sampling strategies
Kinodynamic planning: steering functions and planning with dynamics
Path post-processing: shortcutting and smoothing

units.title: Trajectory generation and optimisation
topics: Trajectory representations: polynomials, splines and minimum-jerk motion
Time-optimal path parametrisation under velocity and torque limits
Optimisation formulations: direct shooting, collocation and constraints
CHOMP, STOMP and TrajOpt: gradient and sequential convex methods for collision-free trajectories
Model predictive control for trajectory tracking with constraints
Combining sampling-based initialisation with optimisation-based refinement

units.title: Differential inverse kinematics
topics: Resolved-rate control, Jacobian pseudo-inverse and damped least squares
Singularities and the manipulability ellipsoid
Redundancy resolution: null-space projection and secondary objectives such as joint limits and obstacle avoidance
Task-priority control and quadratic-programming based inverse kinematics with constraints
Operational-space control and task-space impedance

units.title: Grasp planning
topics: Contact models: point contact with friction, friction cones and the Coulomb model
Form closure, force closure and the grasp matrix
Grasp quality metrics: epsilon-quality and the grasp wrench space
Grasp synthesis: analytic, sampling-based and learned grasp detection from depth images
End-effectors: parallel-jaw, suction and soft grippers, with produce-handling examples from Ghanaian farms and markets
Pick-and-place pipelines and integrated task and motion planning

units.title: Contact-rich manipulation
topics: Compliance: impedance and admittance control
Hybrid force and position control
Contact dynamics: complementarity, friction models and simulation of contact
Insertion and assembly: peg-in-hole, jamming and compliant strategies
Learning for contact-rich tasks: reinforcement learning, demonstration and sim-to-real transfer

units.title: Mobile manipulation
topics: Combining base and arm: whole-body motion and reachability maps
Task and motion planning with symbolic planners and PDDL
Uncertainty: perception errors, belief-space planning and replanning
Nonholonomic base control and docking at a workspace
Software stacks and deployment: MoveIt-style pipelines and field robots for farms and warehouses

units.title: Benchmarking, literature and project
topics: Planner benchmarking: success rate, time, path length and statistical comparison
Reading recent literature: learned planners, diffusion policies and foundation models for manipulation
Safety, verification and failure modes of planners
Project presentation and critique

schedule.title: Configuration space and collision checking
schedule.exercise: Draw the C-space of a two-link planar arm among a rectangular obstacle, compute the Minkowski sum for a polygon robot, and classify four planning problems by class.

tasks.title: Compute the Minkowski sum of a triangular robot and a square obstacle and plot the C-obstacle with the robot reference point
Sample the configuration space of a two-link arm among a box obstacle, plot the colliding region in joint angles, and spot the wrap-around at 2 pi
Implement GJK for two convex polygons, test 100 random pairs against exhaustive edge intersection checks and report any disagreements

schedule.title: Graph search for planning
schedule.exercise: Plan across a grid map with A-star, show when an inadmissible heuristic gives a suboptimal path, and sketch a visibility graph for a polygon map.

tasks.title: Step A-star through an 8 by 8 grid with obstacles, record the open list at each step and compare nodes expanded with Dijkstra
Step D-star Lite as an obstacle appears on the route, and count how many cells it recomputes against replanning from scratch
Build a visibility graph for a polygon map, run Dijkstra on it and compare the path length with grid A-star at three resolutions

schedule.title: Potential fields, lattices and bug algorithms
schedule.exercise: Show a local minimum of a potential field in a U-shaped trap, generate a Dubins path between two poses, and trace Bug2 on a map.

tasks.title: Move a point robot on an attractive-repulsive potential field around two obstacles and plot the path, noting any local minimum it hits
Compute the shortest Dubins path between two poses for a minimum turning radius of 2 m and verify its length against the six word types
Step Bug2 through three obstacle layouts, including one where it circles the obstacle, and measure path length against the optimum

schedule.title: Probabilistic roadmaps and RRT
schedule.exercise: Build a PRM and an RRT on the same map, compare their query times, and explain why RRT-star improves path cost over time.

tasks.title: Grow an RRT in a 2D map with a step size of 0.5 for 500 iterations and watch how the tree reaches the goal region
Build a PRM with 300 nodes, connect each to its 10 nearest neighbours, and answer 20 queries, reporting success rate and path cost
Implement RRT-star with rewiring, plot path cost against iterations for 20 runs and compare with plain RRT cost

schedule.title: Completeness, kinodynamics and smoothing
schedule.exercise: Test planners on a map with a narrow passage, plan for a car-like robot with a steering function, and shortcut a jagged path.

tasks.title: Shortcut a jagged RRT path by repeatedly connecting random pairs of waypoints with collision-free segments and report the length reduction
Measure the success rate of RRT and PRM as the width of a narrow passage shrinks, and compare uniform with bridge-test sampling
Implement a kinodynamic RRT for a car with limited steering angle and test whether the resulting path is drivable by simulation

schedule.title: Trajectory representation and time parametrisation
schedule.exercise: Fit a minimum-jerk trajectory through waypoints, find the time-optimal speed profile along a path under torque limits, and formulate a collocation problem.

tasks.title: Fit a quintic polynomial between two joint positions with zero velocity and acceleration at both ends and plot position, velocity and acceleration
Compute a time-optimal speed profile along a fixed path with velocity and acceleration limits using forward and backward passes
Pose a direct collocation problem for a two-link arm swing-up, solve it with a gradient solver and check the dynamics at the knot points

schedule.title: Optimisation-based planners and MPC
schedule.exercise: Compare CHOMP with a refined sampling-based path on a cluttered scene and write a note on when optimisation fails.

tasks.title: Run a CHOMP-style gradient step on a straight path that crosses an obstacle and plot the path movement over 20 iterations
Track a reference trajectory with a model predictive controller on a double integrator with input limits and plot the tracking error
Initialise an optimiser from an RRT path, refine it, and compare cost and clearance against plain RRT smoothing over 10 maps

schedule.title: Differential kinematics and redundancy
schedule.exercise: Drive a three-link arm to a target with resolved-rate control, show behaviour near a singularity with pseudo-inverse and damped least squares, and use the null space for joint limit avoidance.

tasks.title: Compute the Jacobian of a two-link arm at three poses and find the joint rates that give a desired end-effector velocity
Move a two-link arm through a singular configuration with pseudo-inverse and damped least squares and plot the joint velocity spikes
Control a 3-link redundant arm to a target while using null-space motion to stay away from joint limits and an obstacle point

schedule.title: Grasp mechanics and quality
schedule.exercise: Draw friction cones for a two-finger grasp of a bottle, test force closure for three grasps, and compute a quality metric.

tasks.title: Draw the friction cone for a contact with friction coefficient 0.5 and check whether given contact forces lie inside it
Build the grasp matrix for a three-contact planar grasp and test force closure by checking the origin lies in the interior of the wrench hull
Compute the epsilon grasp quality for 50 candidate grasps of a polygon object and rank them, verifying the best against a perturbation test

schedule.title: Grasp synthesis and pick-and-place
schedule.exercise: Choose end-effectors for picking tomatoes, yams and cartons in a market, and write the plan of a pick-and-place pipeline with failure recovery.

tasks.title: Choose a gripper type for six objects from a Ghanaian market stall and justify each against fragility, shape and surface
Sample antipodal grasps on a depth-map outline, filter by friction cone and report the fraction that pass for three objects
Step a task planner for a block-stacking pick-and-place problem, finding the action sequence and inserting a regrasp when the motion planner fails

schedule.title: Compliance and contact
schedule.exercise: Tune an impedance controller for a wall-contact task, design a peg-in-hole insertion strategy with compliance, and read two papers on learned contact-rich skills.

tasks.title: Plot the response of a mass-spring-damper impedance model hitting a wall for three stiffness values and read the peak contact force
Simulate hybrid force and position control that wipes a surface at constant 5 N force and report the force error along the path
Simulate peg-in-hole insertion with lateral error and a compliant wrist, finding the largest misalignment that still succeeds without jamming

schedule.title: Mobile manipulation and deployment
schedule.exercise: Plan a mobile manipulator that fetches an item from a shelf, with a reachability map, base placement and a recovery plan for a failed grasp.

tasks.title: Plot the reachable workspace of a two-link arm and choose base positions from which a table-top target is reachable
Step a symbolic planner on a fetch-and-carry task with three rooms and two objects, and list the action sequence found
Plan with a noisy object pose estimate, replan when a grasp misses, and measure task success over 100 randomised trials

schedule.title: Benchmarking and project presentation
schedule.exercise: Present the project: problem, planners compared, benchmark design, statistical results and failure analysis, followed by a critique of a peer project.

tasks.title: Run two planners on 20 random maps and tabulate success rate, planning time and path length for each
Compare planner path lengths across 30 maps with a paired test and effect size, and state which planner is preferable
Stress-test your planner with adversarial maps and sensor noise, categorise every failure and propose a fix for the most common one
